name: Late-rent detection and Schedule E auto-ledger for 1–10 unit landlords
pain: Small landlords check bank apps daily or copy numbers from portals into Excel every week. One reports about 600 hours over 3 years. Full PM suites feel bloated or rigid, so many go back to spreadsheets and then forget to update them.
who_pays: US landlords with 1–10 units who already buy spreadsheet templates or pay for PM apps
pay_signal: Weekly 2–4 hour manual updates (86). Rent roll and Schedule E templates are sold on Etsy (487). Users dislike paid apps as overkill or rigid (92,141,151). People are drowning in multiple spreadsheets (148).
product_idea: Lightweight web app built for under 10 units. The landlord forwards payment notification emails (Zelle, Venmo, portal) or uploads a bank CSV. Claude matches payments to tenants and tags expenses to Schedule E lines. A Telegram or email alert fires the morning rent is late. Exports a Schedule E per property.
known_competitors: Stessa, Baselane, TurboTenant, Avail, RentRedi, Etsy spreadsheet templates; crowded at the top, but the 'no bank-link, alert-first' angle is thinner
check_next: Search r/Landlord for complaints about Stessa/Baselane bank sync and late-rent alerts. Test whether landlords will forward payment emails instead of linking a bank.

crowding.reason: Stessa, Baselane and Landlord Studio already auto-tag Schedule E and track rent for free at under 10 units, with paid tiers people buy; the 'no bank link, alert first' angle is a different way in, not an unmet need.

name: Vendor COI and recurring inspection due-date tracker for small property managers
pain: Managers build their own sheets to track vendor certificates of insurance and fire/life-safety inspection cycles (extinguishers, backflow, hoods, alarms). Missed dates mean fines or failed inspections. NetVendor ignores small PMs.
who_pays: Small residential and commercial property management companies (1–50 buildings)
pay_signal: NetVendor, a paid service, effectively turned away a new PM (96), who calls DIY spreadsheets a last resort. Missed inspections cause fines (97). A user built a custom COI sheet after finding nothing decent (90).
product_idea: Upload COI PDFs; Claude extracts the insurer, coverage limits, additional insured and expiry date. Automated emails ask vendors for renewed COIs before expiry. A per-property inspection calendar sends Telegram or email reminders. Self-serve at $29–79/month.
known_competitors: NetVendor, myCOI, Jones, TrustLayer (enterprise and sales-led); PM suites have weak COI modules
check_next: Price-check myCOI and TrustLayer minimums. Post the COI sheet columns from 90 and ask commenters whether they'd pay for auto-extraction plus vendor chasing.

crowding.reason: Several self-serve COI trackers with automated renewal requests already sell at $0–79/month, and BCS has a free tier for up to 25 vendors that reportedly includes AI extraction; the inspection-calendar half was not checked.

name: PDF statement and invoice to spreadsheet extraction for bookkeepers
pain: Bookkeepers retype vendor invoice totals and old bank statement transactions from PDFs, which eats the first week of each month. Bank feeds don't reach far enough back, and QBO/Xero matching fails on real-world transactions.
who_pays: Freelance bookkeepers and small firms doing catch-up and cleanup work
pay_signal: PDF retyping takes up the first week of the month (102). 40+ billable hours went to a 450-transaction catch-up (110). A user asks for a low-cost extraction tool (202). People fall back to spreadsheets despite paying for QBO and Xero (200).
product_idea: Drag-drop batch PDF statements and invoices into a web app. Claude extracts the transactions into a QBO/Xero-ready CSV with running-balance checks to flag extraction errors. Bundle a duplicate and missing-entry finder for cleaning up historical reconciliations.
known_competitors: DocuClipper, ProperSoft, Dext, Hubdoc, AutoEntry, Nanonets; crowded, so differentiate on catch-up cleanup and balance verification
check_next: Run 20 real bank statement PDFs through Claude and measure accuracy. Check DocuClipper pricing per page versus our near-zero AI cost.

crowding.reason: At least 5 paid PDF statement/invoice-to-CSV/QBO converters with public pricing exist (DocuClipper, ProperConvert, MoneyThumb, Bank Statement Converter, Dext) plus Hubdoc free with Xero, and balance-reconciliation checks are already a headline feature; only the duplicate/missing-entry cleanup angle is unverified.

name: Spotify playlist curator growth analytics
pain: Curators can't tell why followers drop or which added tracks helped. Indie artists log release and promo results in spreadsheets by hand.
who_pays: Independent playlist curators and indie artists or small labels running playlist pitching
pay_signal: A curator tracks manually in spreadsheets and notes (172). 80% of release time goes to admin, including updating the curator spreadsheet (164). $400 went to promo with outcomes logged in a spreadsheet (158).
product_idea: Connect playlists through the Spotify API to get daily follower snapshots and an add/remove history. The app correlates follower changes with track changes. Telegram alerts fire on drops or spikes. An artist view tracks which playlists their song landed on and for how long.
check_next: Confirm the Spotify Web API still exposes follower counts and track lists for third-party playlists after the 2024 API restrictions. Price Artist.Tools.

crowding.reason: artist.tools already gives curators daily follower charts, full add/remove history, a playlist dashboard and campaign tracking for $15/mo, and PlaylistSupply, Viberate, Songstats and Chartmetric cover the rest cheaply; only the follower/track correlation and Telegram alerts are missing, which is a feature, not a product.

name: Post-production paperwork generator (TC script, cue sheets, shot lists with thumbnails)
pain: Editors hand-build distributor-required TCScripts or post-production scripts. These list every music, dialogue and footage cue with in and out timecodes. Editors also can't easily get framegrab thumbnails next to timecodes in Sheets, and they track review rounds in Premiere description fields.
who_pays: Freelance documentary and commercial editors and post supervisors facing distributor deliverables
pay_signal: A first TCScript for a distributor is 'absolutely killing' one editor (183). Avid's marker export can't put framegrabs in Sheets (174). A 20-year post supervisor is still juggling spreadsheets and email chains (182). Translation versioning is done by hand (188).
product_idea: Upload an EDL, AAF or XML plus a proxy export. The tool outputs a formatted post-production script: transcribed dialogue (Claude), music cues with durations, and a footage source list. It also outputs a shot list with thumbnails and a VFX turnover sheet, exported to XLSX or Google Sheets.
known_competitors: EDL-X, Cue sheet tools like RightsUp and Soundmouse (music only), Simon Says, Avid ScriptSync
check_next: Ask r/editors which distributor templates (BBC, Netflix, Arte) are most requested. Test parsing Avid and Premiere EDLs plus Whisper or Claude for the dialogue column.

crowding.reason: Free tools (EditingTools.io, Filmscribe, Autocuesheet, KlausVFX) already cover cue sheets, VFX sheets and frame grabs from EDL/XML, and Closed Caption Creator exports CCSLs; only a narrow full-TCScript self-serve gap remains, with no price or payment proof found for it.

name: Offline drive archive catalog for videographers and editors
pain: Editors and wedding videographers with 20+ archive drives can't tell what's on each drive without plugging it in. They keep a Google sheet per drive by hand.
who_pays: Freelance editors, wedding and event videographers with drive closets
pay_signal: An editor of nearly 20 years maintains a manual spreadsheet per drive (178). A videographer asks how others do this at scale (27). Existing catalog apps either cost money or are bad (14). Users dread manually organizing files after shoots (32).
product_idea: Small desktop scanner that indexes a drive, pulls video metadata and poster frames, and uploads the index to a searchable web catalog. Search by client, date or camera. Auto-generates a printable drive label. One-time $39 or a cheap subscription.

name: Venue blog post generator for wedding photographers (SEO pipeline)
pain: Organic social reach for still photos has collapsed. Blogging reliably brings leads, but writing a venue post per wedding with credits and alt text is time-consuming. Vendor contacts sit scattered across emails and business cards.
who_pays: Solo wedding photographers already paying for galleries, CRMs and courses
pay_signal: One photographer gets leads within a day or two of every blog post (40). Venue blog courses and guides are sold to photographers (329). Viewers call SEO tips invaluable (328). There are recurring workarounds for vendor and gallery handoff tracking (47,42).
product_idea: Upload 15–25 selects plus the venue name and vendor list. Claude writes an SEO venue post with venue details, a vendor credits block and per-image alt text and filenames. It exports to WordPress or Showit, and a vendor rolodex builds up from the credits.
known_competitors: Narrative Publish (layout, not writing), generic AI writers, SEO courses like Photography Workflows
check_next: Ask 10 wedding photographers how long a venue post takes them. Check whether Narrative Publish has added AI text and what it charges.

crowding.reason: Only kits, courses and DIY Claude guides compete, and none combine writing, alt text, filenames, export and a vendor list, while photographers already pay for venue-blog AI and SEO courses; my search was cut short.
